question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the plane $y=3x+2z$ that is subject to the constraints ${x}^{2}+{z}^{2}\le 16,\,x\le 0$ and $z\ge 0.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $y=f(x,z)$ with $(x,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
y=3x+2z,\,(x,z)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}\le 16,\,x\le 0,\,z\ge 0},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119930/assets/48ffe2b0bd40937205d9b9d3b6cc264f83bd56ea30a5df318ba7c7507efb68f7.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂y}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x+2z)=3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(3x+2z)=2,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(3)^{2}+(2)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+9+4}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region $D$ can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 4,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \pi }.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula for polar coordinates, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\sqrt{14}\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\,\text{d}\theta {\int }_{0}^{4}r\,\text{d}r \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [\theta ]_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\cdot {[\frac{{r}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 8 \\  & =4\pi \sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$
